findings.finding: S3 and S6 both edit the same close-guard and AC-checkbox-precheck test files with coupled expectations, but neither declares an ordering dependency on the other: S6 renames the expected user-visible message strings (e.g. test_attested_close_guard.py:55, test_ac_checkbox_precheck.py:80, test_ac_checkbox_precheck_heldout.py:235) to name [non-codebase], while S3 parametrizes those same suites over both spellings asserting identical outcomes. If S3's parametrized assertions are written against the pre-rename message strings, they contradict S6's rename; if written against the new strings, S3 silently depends on S6 landing first.

The plan's 'missing half of a pair' rationale refers to the author TAG pair [codebase]/[operator-attested], not the wire `kind` pair codebase-verifiable/operator-attested; renaming one half leaves an asymmetric pair and no stated emit target
findings.finding: The completion-verdict `kind` field is a paired two-value enum (`codebase-verifiable | operator-attested`), but the plan renames only the `operator-attested` half to `non-codebase`, yielding the incoherent emit pairing `codebase-verifiable | non-codebase`; the plan never specifies whether the LLM verifier should now EMIT `non-codebase` (matching the reader-widen) or keep emitting `operator-attested`, so the emitted-value vocabulary is left undefined.
findings.location: Scope decisions: 'the completion-verdict `kind` wire value "operator-attested" -> "non-codebase"'; contracts.py:116; completion_verdict.schema.json:49; completion_verifier.md:224
scenarios: The verifier LLM, told the tag is now [non-codebase] but shown a `kind` vocabulary of `codebase-verifiable | operator-attested`, cannot tell which token to emit into `kind`
A new verdict emits `kind: "operator-attested"` while author guidance shows only `[non-codebase]`, so audit-page badges and the vocabulary drift apart

evidence: Plan: 'All four deterministic consumers share the IDENTICAL compiled regex object — verified: decide_ops, workflow_ops, det_attestation_launder, and det_measurement_provenance each satisfy `is` against det_operator_attested._OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE. Widening that ONE pattern propagates everywhere with no other code change'
src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:544: `from rebar.llm.plan_review.det_operator_attested import _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE`

src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:547: `offenders = [ln for ln in floor.unchecked_ac_lines if not _OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE.match(ln)]` inside `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` — the pre-close AC-checkbox precheck AC3 names ('the AC-checkbox precheck, and the close path')
findings.finding: The plan enumerates a CLOSED set of exactly four deterministic consumers of the shared compiled regex `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` (decide_ops, workflow_ops, det_attestation_launder, det_measurement_provenance) and concludes widening it 'propagates everywhere with no other code change.' A grep sweep for `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` shows a fifth consumer the inventory omits: `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:544-547` (`ensure_ac_boxes_checked`), which imports the compiled object and calls `.match(ln)` in the pre-close AC-checkbox precheck — the exact close-path surface AC3 names. The shared-object claim means the widening still reaches it, but the enumerated consumer set is incomplete and was not derived from a full symbol-reference sweep of the regex name.
findings.location: 'What makes this tractable' — 'All four deterministic consumers share the IDENTICAL compiled regex object … decide_ops, workflow_ops, det_attestation_launder, and det_measurement_provenance'
scenarios: src/rebar/_commands/txn.py `ensure_ac_boxes_checked` — the fifth `_OPERATOR_ATTESTED_TAG_RE` consumer; if the AC3 close-path parametrization test enumerates only the named four, this actual close-path precheck goes unverified for `[non-codebase]`, so a regression that fails to widen it (or a future divergence from object-sharing) would silently block closing `[non-codebase]`-tagged tickets with no test catching it.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the 'four deterministic consumers' sentence to five, naming `_commands/txn.py:ensure_ac_boxes_checked`, and point the AC3 close-path test explicitly at it.
